fieldMarks: Small, mostly aquatic turtle; olive-green to olive-brown shell mottled with dark spots; adult carapace 75-150 mm.
Yellow plastron, greyish-black legs, usually a yellow line along the edge of the front legs.
Green-grey head with dark side stripes and dark spots on chin and crown.
Plastron hinged front and rear, long chin barbels, webbed feet (as described for the Sonoyta subspecies).
behavior: Solitary outside breeding, with overlapping home ranges and very high local densities (over 3,000 per hectare recorded in New Mexico).
Most active in summer monsoon, least active in winter; may estivate on land 11-34 days and move overland up to 8 km.
Eats snails, fish, frogs, crayfish, aquatic insects and occasionally lizards and snakes.
habitat: Streams, springs, ponds and pools in intermittent streams, from desert to oak, pinyon-juniper and pine woodland; in southeastern Arizona about 90% of captures were in stock tanks.
range: Southern and central Arizona and southwestern New Mexico (Catron, Grant, Hidalgo counties), south into Sonora and Chihuahua, Mexico; considered extirpated from California.
